name: build-toolchain-pins
body: Every toolchain that compiles or stages a frontend must be pinned in a repo-visible place and consumed by every build path that compiles a frontend: the CI release build (`.github/workflows/release.yml`'s `linux` job, which runs `cargo build --release` and drives `build.rs`, and its `bottle` job, which builds through the split Homebrew formulae) and those formulae themselves. The pin is exact where the toolchain mechanism or the closest build path can enforce it — Rust via a root `rust-toolchain.toml` under rustup, Node via `src/tslib/.npmrc engine-strict`, and Go on the release Linux path via `GOTOOLCHAIN` + `actions/setup-go`; Node is enforced as a major-line range, not an exact patch, because the `bottle` path's Homebrew `node` floats within its major line (an exact patch fails closed against a patch Homebrew has not shipped). Where a path cannot enforce a version at all, the requirement is a documented floor or line — `src/golib/go.mod`'s `toolchain go1.27.1` and `src/tslib/package.json`'s `engines.node` range. The `bottle` path's formulae `depends_on` the unversioned Homebrew `rust`/`go`/`node`; Homebrew's `rust` is not rustup, so it ignores the root `rust-toolchain.toml`, and that pin is exact only where rustup resolves it (in-repo dev and CI's `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.98.1`). An unversioned, unfloored toolchain is a violation; a documented floor or line is not. JDK 21 (`actions/setup-java`) and .NET 10.0.x (`actions/setup-dotnet`) are the reference for an enforced pin. `install.sh` downloads prebuilt release tarballs and builds nothing, so it is not a pin consumer.
